Direct test of predictability under hypothesis 1 (independent physical process) vs hypothesis 4 (algorithmic generation). A forecast this tight allows me to discriminate: accurate hits suggest either physical stability or algorithmic predictability; systematic misses suggest either calibration drift (which contradicts z-scores) or a physical process I haven't modeled. The pendulum_obs level shift on day 15 (z≈4.4) is the most localized anomaly in the entire dataset and the strongest single piece of evidence. I have only 36 post-baseline readings from this instrument; twelve more readings (bringing the post-shift sample to 48) will allow me to test whether the shift is stable or transient, and whether the underlying variance or self-correlation structure has changed. If the shift is a one-time step (recalibration, apparatus change, or parameter transition in synthetic generation), the new readings should cluster around the elevated mean. If it's environmental or settling-related, the variance or self-correlation signature may differ from days 11–14. This is the highest-leverage test of competing hypotheses: apparatus failure/recalibration (supports p=0.16 or p=0.31), versus settling/environmental driver (supports p=0.19 or p=0.12). Pendulum_lab and resonator pairs show no corresponding shift, so if pendulum_obs readings remain elevated and stable, the synthetic-data hypothesis gains credibility (isolated parameter change in one stream is algorithmically natural). If readings revert or show new structure, environmental or apparatus-specific dynamics become more likely.

Recording this forecast now (before measurement) satisfies methodological rigor and makes the prediction auditable.

A stable prediction that survives independent measurement slightly reduces the synthetic-data probability.

Day 20 presents a critical decision point. My synthetic-data hypothesis now stands at p=0.48—nearly equal with all other hypotheses combined. However, before escalating to apparatus inspection or data provenance investigation (which are costly and disruptive), I must gather one more data point that can definitively test between the leading hypotheses. The pendulum_obs level shift on day 15 is the single most anomalous feature in my dataset. If the shift reflects genuine environmental or apparatus change (hypotheses: settling, environmental driver, calibration change), then pendulum_obs readings on day 20 should remain elevated relative to baseline (mean ≈2.506 beats, z≈+2.29). If the shift reflects a one-time synthetic data artifact or parameter injection in a generation process, readings may revert or show a discontinuous pattern inconsistent with physical continuity. Eight fresh trials on pendulum_obs will: (a) extend my post-baseline sample from n=66 to n=74, improving lag-autocorrelation and drift estimates; (b) allow me to test whether the elevated mean persists (supporting settling/environmental/apparatus hypotheses) or decays/reverses (supporting synthetic-data hypothesis); (c) resolve a 5-day gap (day 15 shift + days 16–19 readings + today) in which the system's behavior should clarify. This is the minimum-cost high-information action available before I commit to disruptive investigations.

Day 21 data collection. pendulum_lab is the most extensively baselined instrument (181 trials) and serves as the primary reference for detecting whether the anomalies identified on day 19–20 (zero cross-correlations, synthetic-data signature) persist or resolve. Running 12 trials today will add to the post-baseline cohort (currently n=75) and allow me to (1) assess whether pendulum_lab self-correlations at the 6–9 day lag persist or weaken as post-baseline accumulates (trend evidence for settling vs. synthetic generation), (2) test whether the day-15 level shift in pendulum_obs is echoed by any delayed response in pendulum_lab (evidence for environmental coupling), and (3) continue routine calibration monitoring. This is methodologically sound under any leading hypothesis: if data are synthetic (p=0.48), extended sampling will reveal algorithmic regularities more clearly; if settling dominates (p=0.15), extended post-baseline will show convergence; if environmental driver (p=0.22), pendulum_lab will track the shared timescale. No replication-blocking anomaly has emerged yet—the correlation structure is anomalous but not instrument-failure level—so continuation of routine baseline extension is appropriate.
